contexts.text: Lives according to a conscience of right. The right and the truth... he believes simply...

Justice is predicated of what is just, and judgment of what is right... There is what is right when a thing is judged from the law, and thus from the justness of the law, thus also according to conscience, because it has the law for its rule.

In the rectitude of my heart () = that it was so thought from innocence and simple good... Rectitude,in the Original, is expressed by a word which means also integrity and perfection, and also simplicity. AC 2529.
Peace and uprightness () = both (the good of Divine love and its truth).
We are right () = that they are truths in themselves. Explained. AC 5437. AC 5460.
Right = truth.
Thou hast rightly spoken () = that it is so from truth.
Charity... is to do what is right in every work. Explained.
Consequently, what is just and right, is the neighbour.
To do what is right () = to live according to the dictate of truth.
Rectitudes () = that which is from the truths of faith.
Truths and right things are there presented as things linear and triangular.
Moral truths relate to... what is sincere and right...
What is sincere and right is of moral life...
By sincerity is meant rectitude, etc.
Unless anyone is interiorly right, etc., he is not right. Illustrated.
He who lives well, and believes rightly, is saved.
One kind of perception is that of what is just and right... and is for man in the world.
Good and truth can inflow into what is just and right, as into their correspondent.
Those who have a perception of what is right (as distinguished from a perception of what is just). Explained.
To lead them in a right way () = into genuine truth. AE 730:37.
The right foot () = the Natural as to good.
The truth of good is signified by, The Word of Jehovah is right ().
To shoot in darkness at the upright in heart () = to deceive those who are in truths from good.
Behold the upright () is said of truth.
Rectitudes () = truths. AE 741:13. AE 741:14.
To wander from the truths of doctrine, and thence no truth in the life, is signified by, Truth stumbleth in the street, and rectitude cannot come ().
A sceptre of rectitude () = the Divine truth which has power and the kingdom;.
Every man who makes what is straight appear crooked, and what is crooked straight (is meant in the eighth commandment).
